title: Smooth principal localization: the localized conormal sequence of a presentation is split exact
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n\ge0$, $P=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $I\subseteq P$ an ideal and $A=P/I$; the conormal module $I/I^2$ is an $A$-module. Let $\mathrm d:I/I^2\to\bigoplus_{i=1}^nA\,\mathrm dx_i$ (the free $A$-module on symbols $\mathrm dx_1,\dots,\mathrm dx_n$) be the $A$-linear map $\mathrm d(g\bmod I^2)=\sum_{i=1}^n\overline{\partial g/\partial x_i}\,\mathrm dx_i$, with $\partial/\partial x_i$ the formal partial derivatives [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative] and the bar the image in $A$. Let $a\in A$ be such that the localization $A_a$ is a smooth $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], and let $\mathrm d_a:(I/I^2)_a\to\bigoplus_{i=1}^nA_a\,\mathrm dx_i$ be the localization of $\mathrm d$ at $a$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. Then (1) $\mathrm d_a$ has an $A_a$-linear left inverse (in particular it is injective); (2) the $A_a$-linear map $\pi:\bigoplus_{i=1}^nA_a\,\mathrm dx_i\to\Omega_{A_a/R}$, $\mathrm dx_i\mapsto\mathrm d(\bar x_i/1)$ ($\Omega_{A_a/R}$ and its derivation as in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]), is surjective with kernel the image of $\mathrm d_a$. Hence $0\to(I/I^2)_a\xrightarrow{\mathrm d_a}\bigoplus_{i=1}^nA_a\,\mathrm dx_i\xrightarrow{\pi}\Omega_{A_a/R}\to0$ is a split short exact sequence and $(I/I^2)_a\oplus\Omega_{A_a/R}\cong A_a^{\oplus n}$ as $A_a$-modules.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07EZ (lemma-compare-standard), part (e), first sentence ('By assumption we have a short exact sequence 0 -> (I/I^2)_a -> (+) A_a dx_i -> Omega_{A_a/R} -> 0 which is split exact'); the same argument in the proof of Lemma Tag 07C6 (lemma-find-strictly-standard, lines 160-170). It rests on Algebra, Lemma Tag 00S1 (lemma-NL-homotopy: the naive cotangent complex of any presentation is homotopy equivalent to NL_{A/R}), Lemma Tag 00S7 (lemma-localize-NL), Lemma Tag 08JZ (lemma-principal-localization-NL) and Definition Tag 00T2 (definition-smooth)

proof.text: Choose $h\in P$ mapping to $a\in A$, and let $\beta:P[x_0]\to A_a$ extend the presentation $P\to A$ by $x_0\mapsto1/a$; write $I'=\ker\beta$. By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-naive-cotangent], $\beta$ is surjective and $I'$ is generated by $I$ and $hx_0-1$. The polynomial algebra $P[x_0]=R[x_1,\dots,x_n,x_0]$ is smooth over $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-smooth]. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-quotient-smooth], applied to $R\to P[x_0]\to A_a=P[x_0]/I'$, gives an exact sequence $$0\to H_1(L_{A_a/R})\to I'/I'^2\xrightarrow{\ d_\beta\ }\Omega_{P[x_0]/R}\otimes_{P[x_0]}A_a\xrightarrow{\ pi_\beta\ }\Omega_{A_a/R}\to0.$$ Since $A_a$ is smooth over $R$, [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] gives $H_1(L_{A_a/R})=0$ and makes $\Omega_{A_a/R}$ a finite projective $A_a$-module. Thus $d_\beta$ is injective, $\pi_\beta$ is surjective, and $\ker\pi_\beta=\operatorname{im}d_\beta$.

source.place: Algebra, Definition Tag 00T2 (definition-smooth, lines 37084-37109), applied to the presentation of the principal localization from Lemma Tag 08JZ (lemma-principal-localization-NL, lines 35605-35629); exactness and the displayed maps are Lemma Tag 00S2 specialized as in lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-quotient-smooth

proof.text: Clause (3) and the final assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-naive-cotangent] identify the complex of step 1 with the direct sum of the localized complex $$(I/I^2)_a\xrightarrow{\ d_a\ }\Omega_{P/R}\otimes_PA_a$$ and the contractible complex $A_a\xrightarrow{\ a\ }A_a$. Since $a$ is a unit in $A_a$, they show that $d_a$ is injective and that its cokernel is canonically the cokernel of $d_\beta$, namely $\Omega_{A_a/R}$ by step 1. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis], $\Omega_{P/R}\otimes_PA_a=\bigoplus_{i=1}^nA_a\,\mathrm dx_i$; under this identification the quotient map to the cokernel sends $\mathrm dx_i$ to $\mathrm d(\bar x_i/1)$, because both maps are induced by the universal derivation [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. It is therefore exactly $\pi$ from the statement. Consequently $\pi$ is surjective and $\ker\pi=\operatorname{im}d_a$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 08JZ (lemma-principal-localization-NL), especially clause (3) and proof lines 35674-35688; the cokernel map is the conormal sequence preceding Definition Tag 00T2, lines 37093-37109

proof.text: Because $\Omega_{A_a/R}$ is projective (step 1), the surjection $\pi$ has an $A_a$-linear section by [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Hence the middle free module is the direct sum $\ker\pi\oplus\operatorname{im}(s)$. Step 2 identifies $\ker\pi$ with $\operatorname{im}d_a$, and injectivity of $d_a$ identifies this image with $(I/I^2)_a$. Projection to this first summand followed by the inverse of $d_a:(I/I^2)_a\to\operatorname{im}d_a$ is an $A_a$-linear left inverse of $d_a$. Thus the displayed short exact sequence is split and $$(I/I^2)_a\oplus\Omega_{A_a/R}\cong\bigoplus_{i=1}^nA_a\,\mathrm dx_i\cong A_a^{\oplus n}.$$

split_report.summary: Checked the statement against Stacks Algebra Definition 00T2 and Lemma 08JZ, and against the uses in Smoothing Ring Maps 07C6 and 07EZ. Wrote a three-step proof: use the quotient presentation P[x_0] -> A_a and Jacobi-Zariski exactness; transfer injectivity and the cokernel to the localized original presentation through 08JZ; split the surjection onto the projective module of differentials. All ingredients already have DAG nodes, so no new node was created.

lean.statement: theorem smooth_localization_conormal_split [Smooth R B] : ∃ (d : M →ₗ[B] (Fin n → B)) (π : (Fin n → B) →ₗ[B] KaehlerDifferential R B), (∀ (g : I) (i : Fin n), d (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers a) I.Cotangent (I.toCotangent g)) i = algebraMap A B (Ideal.Quotient.mk I (MvPolynomial.pderiv i (g : _)))) ∧ (∀ i : Fin n, π (Pi.single i 1) = KaehlerDifferential.D R B (algebraMap A B (Ideal.Quotient.mk I (MvPolynomial.X i)))) ∧ (∃ l : (Fin n → B) →ₗ[B] M, l.comp d = LinearMap.id) ∧ Function.Injective d ∧ Function.Surjective π ∧ LinearMap.ker π = LinearMap.range d ∧ (∃ s : KaehlerDifferential R B →ₗ[B] (Fin n → B), π.comp s = LinearMap.id) ∧ Nonempty ((M × KaehlerDifferential R B) ≃ₗ[B] (Fin n → B))
lean.note: R, n, I, a are explicitly bound section variables. Local notation A = MvPolynomial (Fin n) R ⧸ I, B = Localization.Away a, M = LocalizedModule.Away a I.Cotangent. The maps are existentially specified by their uniquely determining generator values; no arbitrary map hypothesis is imposed.
